trickyParts: A pull request's CI runs on the merge ref, which carries main's tip rather than the main the branch last merged. So a red check can name a package the branch does not touch and a tree the branch does not hold: the same test passed at the branch's own head throughout. Reading the failure against the branch's tree, not only against the run, is what told the two apart.
The old CI run must not be re-run: a re-run reuses the same merge ref, which still carries main before the fix, so it fails again. Only a new push makes a merge ref over main's new tip.
deviations: This round changed no code and spent no fix attempt on one. The architect held the branch while sjawhar/legion#2598 fixed main, then lifted the hold; the whole round is the forward merge it asked for.
discoveredComplexity: docs/kubernetes.md has no layout gate at all, and the two Envoy guides' gate (bun test scripts/semantic-line-breaks.guides.test.ts) is deliberately out of CI, which is how a reflow that put blank lines between bullets reached main and broke a check that parses one of those lists. That is written up in docs/solutions/testing/the-envoy-guides-layout-checker-runs-only-when-you-run-it-pr2580.md, this pull request's own retro learning, which named the two guides; docs/kubernetes.md is a third file in the same class.
